formula: pred cites[u, v: Unit] { u->v in Sit.rel or u->v in Derive.rel }
statement:
For every unit_1 and every unit_2:

unit_1 cites unit_2 exactly when unit_1 sits in unit_2 or derives from unit_2.

For every unit:

the unit is unfounded exactly when the unit is one of these:
- a spec that cites no axiom and cites no spec
- an exception that cites no spec or cites no fact
- a bug that cites no spec

formula:
pred miscited[u: Unit] {
  (u in Axiom and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v] and v not in Axiom))
  or (u in Fact and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v]))
  or (u in Spec and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v] and v not in Axiom and v not in Spec and v not in Fact))
  or (u in Exception and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v] and v not in Spec and v not in Fact))
  or (u in Bug and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v] and v not in Spec))
  or (u in Conflict and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v]))
  or (u in Term and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v]))
}
statement:
For every unit_1:

unit_1 is miscited exactly when unit_1 is one of these:
- an axiom that cites a unit that is not an axiom
- a fact that cites a unit
- a spec that cites a unit that is not an axiom, a spec or a fact
- an exception that cites a unit that is not a spec or a fact
- a bug that cites a unit that is not a spec
- a conflict that cites a unit
- a term that cites a unit

formula: pred circular[u: Unit] { some v: Unit | cites[u, v] and v->u in Depend.rel }
statement:
For every unit_1:

unit_1 is circular exactly when unit_1 cites a unit that depends on unit_1.

formula: pred refined[c: Claim] { (some s: Spec | s->c in Sit.rel) or (some e: Exception | e->c in Sit.rel) }
statement:
For every claim:

the claim is refined exactly when a spec sits in the claim or an exception sits in the claim.

formula: pred unguarded[c: Claim] { not refined[c] and not tested[c] }
statement:
For every claim:

the claim is unguarded exactly when the claim is not refined and is not tested.

For every test:

the test is adrift exactly when at least one of these holds:
- project declares the test and the test carries no tag
- project declares the test and the test checks a unit that is not a claim
- the test checks a claim that is refined

For every unit_1:

unit_1 is used exactly when another unit sits in unit_1, a pointer names unit_1 or a tag names unit_1.

formula: pred checks[t: Test, u: Unit] { some g: Tag | t->g in Carry.rel and g->u in Name.tag }
statement:
For every test and every unit:

the test checks the unit exactly when the test carries a tag that names the unit.

For every unit:

the unit is tested exactly when at least one of these holds:
- a test checks the unit
- the unit is a spec and a test checks a bug that sits in the unit

formula: pred paired[c: Conflict] { some a, b: Unit | a != b and c->a in Name.between and c->b in Name.between }
statement:
For every conflict:

the conflict is paired exactly when the conflict names a unit and names another unit.

For every unit:

the unit is hidden exactly when at least one of these holds:
- all of these hold:
  - the unit is a bug
  - at least one of these holds:
    - project has a tracker and the unit names no issue
    - the unit names an issue that tracker does not know
    - the unit names an issue that tracker has closed
    - project has a runner and the unit is not tested
- all of these hold:
  - the unit is a conflict
  - at least one of these holds:
    - project has a tracker and the unit names no issue
    - the unit names an issue that tracker does not know
    - the unit names an issue that tracker has closed
    - the unit is not paired

For every test_1:

test_1 is misleading exactly when test_1 is one of these:
- an expected failure that checks no bug and checks no exception
- a plain test that checks a bug

formula: pred lists[f: Frontmatter, p: Plugin] { some e: Entry | f->e in Item.rel and e->p in Spell.rel }
statement:
For every frontmatter and every plugin:

the frontmatter lists the plugin exactly when the frontmatter holds an entry that spells the plugin.

formula: pred applies[p: Plugin, d: Document] { some f: Listing | d->f in Head.rel and lists[f, p] }
statement:
For every plugin and every document:

the plugin applies to the document exactly when the document starts with a listing frontmatter that lists the plugin.

For every run and every plugin:

the run calls the plugin exactly when all of these hold:
- the run asks for a command that the plugin adds
- the plugin applies to a document

For every command_1:

command_1 is available exactly when at least one of these holds:
- command_1 is a command that the checker has of its own
- there are installed_plugin_1 and document_1 such that installed_plugin_1 applies to document_1 and adds command_1

formula:
(all u: Unit | unfounded[u] implies u in Finding)
and (all u: Unit | miscited[u] implies u in Finding)
and (all u: Unit | circular[u] implies u in Finding)
statement:
All of these hold:
- for every unit:

  when the unit is unfounded, checker reports a finding for the unit
- for every unit:

  when the unit is miscited, checker reports a finding for the unit
- for every unit:

  when the unit is circular, checker reports a finding for the unit.

formula: all u: Unit | unfounded[u] implies u in Freelancing
statement:
For every unit:

when the unit is unfounded, checker reports a freelancing for the unit.

formula: all s: Spec | ((no a: Axiom | cites[s, a]) and (no t: Spec | cites[s, t])) implies s in Freelancing
statement:
For every spec_1:

when spec_1 cites no axiom and cites no spec, checker reports a freelancing for spec_1.

formula: all e: Exception | (no s: Spec | cites[e, s]) implies e in Freelancing
statement:
For every exception:

when the exception cites no spec, checker reports a freelancing for the exception.

formula: all e: Exception | (no f: Fact | cites[e, f]) implies e in Freelancing
statement:
For every exception:

when the exception cites no fact, checker reports a freelancing for the exception.

formula: all b: Bug | (no s: Spec | cites[b, s]) implies b in Freelancing
statement:
For every bug:

when the bug cites no spec, checker reports a freelancing for the bug.

formula: all u: Unit | miscited[u] implies u in Misnesting
statement:
For every unit:

when the unit is miscited, checker reports a misnesting for the unit.

formula: all a: Axiom | (some u: Unit | cites[a, u] and u not in Axiom) implies a in Misnesting
statement:
For every axiom_1:

when axiom_1 cites a unit that is not an axiom, checker reports a misnesting for axiom_1.

formula: all f: Fact | (some u: Unit | cites[f, u]) implies f in Misnesting
statement:
For every fact:

when the fact cites a unit, checker reports a misnesting for the fact.

formula: all s: Spec | (some u: Unit | cites[s, u] and u not in Axiom and u not in Spec and u not in Fact) implies s in Misnesting
statement:
For every spec_1:

when the following holds:

spec_1 cites a unit that is not an axiom, a spec or a fact

then checker reports a misnesting for spec_1.

formula: all e: Exception | (some u: Unit | cites[e, u] and u not in Spec and u not in Fact) implies e in Misnesting
statement:
For every exception:

when the exception cites a unit that is not a spec or a fact, checker reports a misnesting for the exception.

formula: all b: Bug | (some u: Unit | cites[b, u] and u not in Spec) implies b in Misnesting
statement:
For every bug:

when the bug cites a unit that is not a spec, checker reports a misnesting for the bug.

formula: all c: Conflict | (some u: Unit | cites[c, u]) implies c in Misnesting
statement:
For every conflict:

when the conflict cites a unit, checker reports a misnesting for the conflict.

formula: all t: Term | (some u: Unit | cites[t, u]) implies t in Misnesting
statement:
For every term:

when the term cites a unit, checker reports a misnesting for the term.

formula: all u: Unit | circular[u] implies u in Cycle
statement:
For every unit:

when the unit is circular, checker reports a cycle for the unit.

formula:
(all b: Bug | hidden[b] implies b in Finding)
and (all c: Conflict | hidden[c] implies c in Finding)
and (all t: Test | misleading[t] implies t in Finding)
statement:
All of these hold:
- for every bug:

  when the bug is hidden, checker reports a finding for the bug
- for every conflict:

  when the conflict is hidden, checker reports a finding for the conflict
- for every test:

  when the test is misleading, checker reports a finding for the test.

formula: all b: Bug | hidden[b] implies b in Finding
statement:
For every bug:

when the bug is hidden, checker reports a finding for the bug.

formula: all b: Bug | (some Tracker and (no i: Issue | b->i in Name.issue)) implies b in Untracking
statement:
For every bug:

when project has a tracker and the bug names no issue, checker reports an untracking for the bug.

formula: all b: Bug | (some i: Issue | b->i in Name.issue and i not in Known) implies b in Mistracking
statement:
For every bug:

when the bug names an issue that tracker does not know, checker reports a mistracking for the bug.

formula: all b: Bug | (some i: Issue | b->i in Name.issue and i in Closed) implies b in OutdatedTracking
statement:
For every bug:

when the bug names an issue that tracker has closed, checker reports an outdated tracking for the bug.

formula: all b: Bug | (some Runner and not tested[b]) implies b in Untesting
statement:
For every bug:

when project has a runner and the bug is not tested, checker reports an untesting for the bug.

formula: all c: Conflict | hidden[c] implies c in Finding
statement:
For every conflict:

when the conflict is hidden, checker reports a finding for the conflict.

formula: all c: Conflict | (some Tracker and (no i: Issue | c->i in Name.issue)) implies c in Untracking
statement:
For every conflict:

when project has a tracker and the conflict names no issue, checker reports an untracking for the conflict.

formula: all c: Conflict | (some i: Issue | c->i in Name.issue and i not in Known) implies c in Mistracking
statement:
For every conflict:

when the conflict names an issue that tracker does not know, checker reports a mistracking for the conflict.

formula: all c: Conflict | (some i: Issue | c->i in Name.issue and i in Closed) implies c in OutdatedTracking
statement:
For every conflict:

when the conflict names an issue that tracker has closed, checker reports an outdated tracking for the conflict.

formula: all c: Conflict | not paired[c] implies c in Unpairing
statement:
For every conflict:

when the conflict is not paired, checker reports an unpairing for the conflict.

formula: all t: Test | misleading[t] implies t in Finding
statement:
For every test:

when the test is misleading, checker reports a finding for the test.

formula: all x: ExpectedFailure | ((no b: Bug | checks[x, b]) and (no e: Exception | checks[x, e])) implies x in UnexplainedFailure
statement:
For every expected failure:

when the expected failure checks no bug and checks no exception, checker reports an unexplained failure for the expected failure.

formula: all t: PlainTest | (some b: Bug | checks[t, b]) implies t in Unpinning
statement:
For every plain test:

when the plain test checks a bug, checker reports an unpinning for the plain test.

formula:
(all c: Claim | (some Runner and unguarded[c]) implies c in Finding)
and (all g: Tag | (no u: Unit | g->u in Name.tag) implies g in Finding)
and (all t: Test | adrift[t] implies t in Finding)
and (all p: Pointer | (no x: Target | p->x in Name.pointer) implies p in Finding)
and (all u: Unit | (not used[u] and u not in Conflict) implies u in Finding)
and (all u: Unit | (some t: Trailer | t->u in Follow.rel) implies u in Finding)
and (all d: Document | ((some u: Unit | d->u in Hold.units) and (no i: Index | d->i in Hold.indexes)) implies d in Finding)
and (all d: Document | (some i: Index | d->i in Hold.indexes and i->d not in Match.rel) implies d in Finding)
and (all c: Claim | (some s: Site | c->s in Name.site and (no r: Source | r->s in Hold.symbols)) implies c in Finding)
and (all u: Unit | (some v: Unit | u->v in Repeat.rel) implies u in Finding)
statement:
All of these hold:
- for every claim:

  when project has a runner and the claim is unguarded, checker reports a finding for the claim
- for every tag:

  when the tag names no unit, checker reports a finding for the tag
- for every test:

  when the test is adrift, checker reports a finding for the test
- for every pointer:

  when the pointer names no target, checker reports a finding for the pointer
- for every unit_1:

  when unit_1 is not used and is not a conflict, checker reports a finding for unit_1
- for every unit_1:

  when a trailer follows unit_1, checker reports a finding for unit_1
- for every document:

  when the document holds a unit and holds no index, checker reports a finding for the document
- for every document:

  when the document holds an index that does not match the document, checker reports a finding for the document
- for every claim:

  when the claim names a site that no source holds, checker reports a finding for the claim
- for every unit_1:

  when unit_1 repeats a unit, checker reports a finding for unit_1.

formula: all c: Claim | (some Runner and unguarded[c]) implies c in Untesting
statement:
For every claim:

when project has a runner and the claim is unguarded, checker reports an untesting for the claim.

formula: all g: Tag | (no u: Unit | g->u in Name.tag) implies g in Rotting
statement:
For every tag:

when the tag names no unit, checker reports a rotting for the tag.

formula: all t: Test | adrift[t] implies t in Finding
statement:
For every test:

when the test is adrift, checker reports a finding for the test.

formula: all t: Test | (t in Declared and (no g: Tag | t->g in Carry.rel)) implies t in Uncitation
statement:
For every test:

when project declares the test and the test carries no tag, checker reports an uncitation for the test.

formula: all t: Test | (t in Declared and (some u: Unit | checks[t, u] and u not in Claim)) implies t in Misaiming
statement:
For every test:

when project declares the test and the test checks a unit that is not a claim, checker reports a misaiming for the test.

formula: all t: Test | (some c: Claim | checks[t, c] and refined[c]) implies t in Overreach
statement:
For every test:

when the test checks a claim that is refined, checker reports an overreach for the test.

formula: all p: Pointer | (no x: Target | p->x in Name.pointer) implies p in Rotting
statement:
For every pointer:

when the pointer names no target, checker reports a rotting for the pointer.

formula: all u: Unit | (some v: Unit | u->v in Repeat.rel) implies u in Rotting
statement:
For every unit_1:

when unit_1 repeats a unit, checker reports a rotting for unit_1.

formula: all u: Unit | (not used[u] and u not in Conflict) implies u in Orphaning
statement:
For every unit:

when the unit is not used and is not a conflict, checker reports an orphaning for the unit.

formula: all u: Unit | (some t: Trailer | t->u in Follow.rel) implies u in Misanchoring
statement:
For every unit:

when a trailer follows the unit, checker reports a misanchoring for the unit.

formula: all d: Document | ((some u: Unit | d->u in Hold.units) and (no i: Index | d->i in Hold.indexes)) implies d in Misindexing
statement:
For every document:

when the document holds a unit and holds no index, checker reports a misindexing for the document.

formula: all d: Document | (some i: Index | d->i in Hold.indexes and i->d not in Match.rel) implies d in Misindexing
statement:
For every document:

when the document holds an index that does not match the document, checker reports a misindexing for the document.

formula: all c: Claim | (some s: Site | c->s in Name.site and (no r: Source | r->s in Hold.symbols)) implies c in Mislocation
statement:
For every claim:

when the claim names a site that no source holds, checker reports a mislocation for the claim.

formula: all d: Document, e: Document, g: Document | (d->e in Extend.rel implies d->e in Context.rel) and ((d->e in Extend.rel and e->g in Context.rel) implies d->g in Context.rel)
statement:
For every document_1 and every document_2 and every document_3:

all of these hold:
- when document_1 extends document_2, document_2 is context for document_1
- when document_1 extends document_2 and document_3 is context for document_2, document_3 is context for document_1

formula: all f: Fence, u: Unit | (f in Languaged and f->u in Within.rel) implies u->f in Blocks.rel
statement:
For every fence_1 and every unit:

when all of these hold:
- fence_1 is a fence that names a language
- fence_1 lies in the own text of the unit

then checker reads fence_1 as a block of the unit.

formula: all f: Fence | f not in Languaged implies (no u: Unit | u->f in Blocks.rel)
statement:
For every fence_1:

when fence_1 is a fence that names no language, checker reads fence_1 as a block of no unit.

formula: all f: Fence | f in VocabularyWord implies f in VocabularyBlock
statement:
For every fence:

when the second word of the fence is vocabulary, the fence has the role of vocabulary.

formula: all f: Fence | f in BoundsWord implies f in BoundsBlock
statement:
For every fence:

when the second word of the fence is bounds, the fence has the role of bounds.

formula: all f: Fence | f in ScenarioWord implies f in ScenarioBlock
statement:
For every fence:

when the second word of the fence is scenario, the fence has the role of scenario.

formula: all f: Fence | f in NoSecondWord implies f in UnitBlock
statement:
For every fence:

when the fence has no second word that names a role, the fence has the role of the formula of its unit.

formula: all f: Fence, u: Unit | f->u in Within.rel implies (no v: Unit | v->u in Sit.rel and v->f in Blocks.rel)
statement:
For every fence and every unit_1:

when the fence lies in the own text of unit_1, checker reads the fence as a block of no unit that sits in unit_1.

formula: all c: Claim | tested[c] implies c not in Untesting
statement:
For every claim:

when the claim is tested, checker reports no untesting for the claim.

formula: all c: Claim | (some t: Test | t in Declared and checks[t, c]) implies c not in Untesting
statement:
For every claim:

when a test that project declares checks the claim, checker reports no untesting for the claim.

formula: all c: Claim | (some t: Test | t not in Declared and checks[t, c]) implies c not in Untesting
statement:
For every claim:

when a test that project does not declare checks the claim, checker reports no untesting for the claim.

formula: all s: Spec | (some t: Test, b: Bug | checks[t, b] and b->s in Sit.rel) implies s not in Untesting
statement:
For every spec:

when a test checks a bug that sits in the spec, checker reports no untesting for the spec.

formula: all u: Unit | no Runner implies u not in Untesting
statement:
For every unit:

when project has no runner, checker reports no untesting for the unit.

formula: all u: Unit | no Tracker implies u not in Untracking
statement:
For every unit:

when project has no tracker, checker reports no untracking for the unit.

formula: all r: Run | ((some f: Frontmatter, p: Missing | lists[f, p]) or (some d: Document | d in Unreadable) or (some c: Command | r->c in Ask.rel and not available[c]) or (some p: Plugin | r->p in Return.code2)) implies r in Exits2
statement:
For every run:

when at least one of these holds:
- there are frontmatter_1 and missing_plugin_1 such that frontmatter_1 lists missing_plugin_1
- there is a document such that checker reports that the document has a frontmatter it cannot read
- the run asks for a command that is not available
- the run gets code 2 from a plugin

then the run exits with code 2.

formula: all p: Plugin, d: Document | (applies[p, d] implies p->d in Over.rel) and ((d not in Given and p->d in Over.rel) implies applies[p, d])
statement:
For every plugin and every document:

all of these hold:
- when the plugin applies to the document, checker runs the plugin over the document
- when the command line of a run does not name the document and checker runs the plugin over the document, the plugin applies to the document

formula: all p: Plugin, d: Document | ((no f: Listing | d->f in Head.rel) and d not in Given) implies p->d not in Over.rel
statement:
For every plugin and every document:

when the document starts with no listing frontmatter and the command line of a run does not name the document, checker does not run the plugin over the document.

formula: all p: Plugin, d: Document, f: Listing | (d->f in Head.rel and lists[f, p]) implies p->d in Over.rel
statement:
For every plugin and every document and every listing frontmatter:

when the document starts with the listing frontmatter and the listing frontmatter lists the plugin, checker runs the plugin over the document.

formula: all p: Plugin, d: Document, f: Listing | (d->f in Head.rel and not lists[f, p] and d not in Given) implies p->d not in Over.rel
statement:
For every plugin and every document and every listing frontmatter:

when all of these hold:
- the document starts with the listing frontmatter
- the listing frontmatter does not list the plugin
- the command line of a run does not name the document

then checker does not run the plugin over the document.

formula: all p: Plugin, d: Document, f: Listing | (d->f in Head.rel and (no e: Entry | f->e in Item.rel) and d not in Given) implies p->d not in Over.rel
statement:
For every plugin and every document and every listing frontmatter:

when all of these hold:
- the document starts with the listing frontmatter
- the listing frontmatter holds no entry
- the command line of a run does not name the document

then checker does not run the plugin over the document.

formula: all r: Run, p: Plugin, d: Given | calls[r, p] implies p->d in Over.rel
statement:
For every run_1 and every plugin and every given document:

when run_1 calls the plugin, checker runs the plugin over the given document.

formula: all f: Frontmatter | f not in Listing implies (no e: Entry | f->e in Item.rel)
statement:
For every frontmatter_1:

when frontmatter_1 is not a frontmatter with a plugins key, frontmatter_1 holds no entry.

formula: all f: Frontmatter | (f in Misquoted or f in Foreign or f in Unclosed or f in Unterminated or f in Doubled or f in Dangling or f in Looping or f in Stray) implies f in Refused
statement:
For every frontmatter_1:

when at least one of these holds:
- frontmatter_1 has the flaw of an entry that starts with an at sign outside quotes
- frontmatter_1 has the flaw of a key that neither the checker nor a plugin that frontmatter_1 lists defines
- frontmatter_1 has the flaw of a list that is not closed
- frontmatter_1 has the flaw of a string that is not closed
- frontmatter_1 has the flaw of a key that appears twice
- frontmatter_1 has the flaw of a path that names no document
- frontmatter_1 has the flaw of an extension that leads back to its own document
- frontmatter_1 has the flaw of a setting in a document that is not the entry document

then frontmatter_1 is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.

formula: all f: Misquoted | f in Refused
statement:
For every misquoted frontmatter:

the misquoted frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.

formula: all f: Foreign | f in Refused
statement:
For every foreign frontmatter:

the foreign frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.

formula: all f: Unclosed | f in Refused
statement:
For every unclosed frontmatter:

the unclosed frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.

formula: all f: Unterminated | f in Refused
statement:
For every unterminated frontmatter:

the unterminated frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.

formula: all f: Doubled | f in Refused
statement:
For every doubled frontmatter:

the doubled frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.

formula: all f: Dangling | f in Refused
statement:
For every dangling frontmatter:

the dangling frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.

formula: all f: Looping | f in Refused
statement:
For every circular frontmatter:

the circular frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.

formula: all f: Stray | f in Refused
statement:
For every stray frontmatter:

the stray frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.

formula: all r: Run, d: Document, f: Refused | d->f in Head.rel implies (d in Unreadable and r in Exits2)
statement:
For every run and every document and every refused frontmatter:

when the document starts with the refused frontmatter,

then all of these hold:
- checker reports that the document has a frontmatter it cannot read
- the run exits with code 2

formula: all d: Document, f: Refused | d->f in Head.rel implies d in Unreadable
statement:
For every document and every refused frontmatter:

when the document starts with the refused frontmatter, checker reports that the document has a frontmatter it cannot read.

formula: all r: Run | (some d: Document | d in Unreadable) implies r in Exits2
statement:
For every run:

when there is a document such that checker reports that the document has a frontmatter it cannot read, the run exits with code 2.

formula: all r: Run, f: Frontmatter, p: Missing | lists[f, p] implies (p in Unfound and r in Exits2)
statement:
For every run and every frontmatter and every missing plugin:

when the frontmatter lists the missing plugin,

then all of these hold:
- checker reports that the project lacks the missing plugin
- the run exits with code 2

formula: all f: Frontmatter, p: Missing | lists[f, p] implies p in Unfound
statement:
For every frontmatter and every missing plugin:

when the frontmatter lists the missing plugin, checker reports that the project lacks the missing plugin.

formula: all r: Run, f: Frontmatter, p: Missing | lists[f, p] implies r in Exits2
statement:
For every run and every frontmatter and every missing plugin:

when the frontmatter lists the missing plugin, the run exits with code 2.

formula: all r: Run, c: Command | (r->c in Ask.rel and not available[c]) implies (c in Unknown and r in Exits2)
statement:
For every run and every command_1:

when the run asks for command_1 and command_1 is not available, checker reports command_1 as an unknown command and the run exits with code 2.

formula: all r: Run, c: Command | (r->c in Ask.rel and not available[c]) implies c in Unknown
statement:
For every run and every command_1:

when the run asks for command_1 and command_1 is not available, checker reports command_1 as an unknown command.

formula: all r: Run, c: Command | (r->c in Ask.rel and not available[c]) implies r in Exits2
statement:
For every run and every command:

when the run asks for the command and the command is not available, the run exits with code 2.

formula: all c: Command | available[c] implies c not in Unknown
statement:
For every command_1:

when command_1 is available, checker does not report command_1 as an unknown command.

formula: all r: Run, p: Plugin | calls[r, p] implies (r->p in Return.code0 or r->p in Return.code1 or r->p in Return.code2)
statement:
For every run and every plugin:

when the run calls the plugin,
